question: Are people more likely to die on their birthday than on an ordinary day?
answer: Yes, a little. Among about 2.4 million Swiss deaths from 1969 to 2008, 13.8% more fell on the birthday than chance predicts, and 18% more among people over 60. The rise was sharpest for heart disease and strokes. Nobody knows why; the excess sits on one square of each person's calendar.
move: An anniversary can change what people do, and that can show up in the records.
source: Ajdacic-Gross et al., Annals of Epidemiology, 2012
